title: Evaluator Set Drift on an Agent Stream
dataSources: The stream's enabled evaluator list from `get_metrics()` compared with the team's expected list
description: Detects evaluators silently turned off on an Agent Stream. `enable_evaluators` replaces the stream's whole set, so a script that adds one evaluator can disable the others.
value: Quality, safety and privacy checks stop without any error when they drop out of the set. Comparing the live set with the expected list catches it the same day.
implementation: Keep the expected evaluator list per stream in configuration. Always pass the full list to `enable_evaluators`. Run a daily check that compares `get_metrics()` with the expected list and reports any difference.
visualization: Check output listing missing or unexpected evaluators per stream.
knownFalsePositives: A planned change to the evaluator set shows as drift until the expected list is updated in the same change.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

No new instrumentation. The check uses the SDK with the same project and stream settings as the agent.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Evaluators are defined for the organization and turned on per Agent Stream, in the console (Configure Evaluators) or with `enable_evaluators`. That SDK call replaces the stream's set: anything left out is turned off. Evaluators run after the trace is stored, on a sample. A 10% rate stores every trace and scores one in ten, and a sampled trace is scored by every enabled evaluator. There is no documented default sample rate, so set it explicitly.

Step 3 — Validate

On a test stream, enable two evaluators, then call `enable_evaluators` with one and confirm the check reports the other as missing. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Run the check daily and after every change to evaluator configuration.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

`get_metrics()` returns names the expected list does not use: align the expected list with the names it returns (for example `tool_selection_quality`).
grandmaExplanation: We keep a checklist of the reviewers that should be watching the assistant and check every day that none has been sent home by mistake.

productArtifacts.title: Compare the stream's evaluators with the expected set
productArtifacts.body:
from splunk_ao import AgentStream

EXPECTED = {"tool_selection_quality"}  # the full set this stream should have

s = AgentStream.get(name=stream_name, project_name=project_name)
live = set(s.get_metrics())
missing, extra = EXPECTED - live, live - EXPECTED
if missing or extra:
    print(f"evaluator drift on {stream_name}: missing={sorted(missing)} extra={sorted(extra)}")
